steps.description:

steps.name: A Sinking Feeling

steps.description:

In financial services, this kind of data exposure could have serious regulatory consequences. You need to contact IT Security right away.

steps.name: What Went Wrong
steps.description:
David from IT Security explained that SmartSync Pro wasn't a legitimate productivity tool - it was a data harvesting application designed to steal corporate information.

But Marcus recommended it. As David said on the call, Marcus's account had been compromised. Alice opens the original message to see what she missed.

steps.name: Examining the Sender

steps.instructions: Click through to review the sender analysis.

steps.name: The Real Problem
steps.description:
As David explained, Marcus's account had been compromised through a phishing attack weeks earlier. The attacker used his account to spread the malicious app recommendation to other employees.

The bigger issue was the OAuth consent screen - you granted far more permissions than a calendar app should need. Let's review what you agreed to.
steps.instructions: Click Next to analyze the permissions you granted.

steps.name: Analyzing the Permissions
steps.note: Malicious apps often request far more permissions than they need. A simple task like 'calendar reminders' should never require email sending or file access.

highlighterTexts: Read and send email on your behalf - A calendar app has no reason to touch email. This let SmartSync Pro download confidential client attachments, and it could have sent phishing emails from Alice's account.
Access all your contacts - A reminder tool doesn't need your full contact list. This permission let SmartSync Pro export Alice's entire list of clients and colleagues to external servers.
Read and write files in your cloud storage - Completely unnecessary for calendar reminders. This gave the app full access to confidential financial documents, client portfolios, and internal reports.
Access your data offline - This allowed SmartSync Pro to continue harvesting data even when Alice wasn't actively using the app. Legitimate apps rarely need this level of persistent access.

steps.description:
David walks Alice through the permissions SmartSync Pro requested. Let's revisit the consent screen and examine each permission that should have raised a red flag.

A legitimate calendar reminder app should only need to read your calendar and send notifications - nothing more.
steps.instructions: Look over the consent screen, then click Next and review each permission that was granted to SmartSync Pro.

steps.name: Permission Check

answers.text: Allow it - the app probably needs all these permissions to function
answers.explanation: Never assume an app needs everything it requests. Email send access and full file access are major red flags for a project management tool.

answers.text: Deny it - the email and file permissions are excessive for a project management tool, and check with IT for an approved alternative
answers.explanation: A project management app has no reason to send emails as you or access all your files. Always deny excessive permissions and check with IT for approved alternatives.

answers.text: Allow it but change your password afterward as a precaution
answers.explanation: Changing your password doesn't help - OAuth tokens work independently of your password. The app would still have access to everything you granted.

answers.text: Allow it since the consent screen is from your company's official portal
answers.explanation: The consent screen being on your company portal only means the app is requesting access through proper channels - it says nothing about whether the app itself is trustworthy or needs those permissions.

steps.name: Understanding OAuth Risks

highlighterTexts: OAuth lets third-party apps access your account without knowing your password.
When you click 'Allow', you grant that app specific permissions to act on your behalf - always read what you're granting.

steps.description: Alice clicks the training link to open the security training portal. The first module explains what OAuth is and how attackers exploit it.
steps.instructions: Click the training link in the email, look the page over, then click Next and review the content.

steps.name: Permission Red Flags
steps.note: Before granting OAuth permissions, always ask: 'Does this app truly need this access to perform its stated function?'

highlighterTexts: Red flags: reading and sending email on your behalf, access to all your contacts, and offline access - few legitimate apps need these.
Always ask: 'Does the app need this?'

steps.description:
The training explains permission red flags to watch for. Its example shows three requests that should make you stop: Red Flags:
  • Read and send email on your behalf - Few legitimate apps need to send emails as you
  • Access all your contacts - Rarely needed for productivity tools
  • Access your data offline - Allows data collection even when you're not actively using the app
Questions to Ask:
  • Does the app need this? A calendar app shouldn't need email send access.
  • Why offline access? This lets the app access data without you being logged in.
  • Full access vs. read-only? Be wary of write permissions when read-only would suffice.
  • Is this from IT? Unapproved apps may not meet security standards.
steps.instructions: Click 'View Safe Practices' to continue.

steps.name: Safe App Authorization Practices

highlighterTexts: Before you connect: read every permission, check who published the app, and grant only what the task needs.
After you connect: re-check your connected apps, and ask IT Security when you are unsure about one.

steps.description:
The training sums up safe practice for third-party apps in five rules:
  • Read every permission - An app asking to send mail as you or delete files wants more than it needs
  • Check who published it - Look up the developer before you grant anything
  • Grant only what the task needs - Excessive access is the app's problem to fix, not yours to accept
  • Re-check connected apps - Access granted once stays granted until you remove it
  • Ask when you are unsure - IT Security would rather answer a question than investigate a breach
steps.instructions: Click 'Complete Training' to finish the module.

steps.name: Training Complete

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Thank you for completing the Third-Party App Security training. I can see you've finished the module.

Quick update on the incident:
  • SmartSync Pro has been completely revoked from your account
  • We've reset your password (you'll be prompted on next login)
  • Client contacts and some attachments were exported before we revoked the app - we are notifying the affected clients
  • Marcus's account has been secured and he's been notified

Going forward, please remember to check our approved apps list before connecting any new tools. If you need a productivity app, submit a request through IT - we can often find a secure alternative.

Thanks for your quick response on this.

David Chen
IT Security Team
email.subject: Training Complete - Thank You

highlighterTexts: The damage was real: client contacts and attachments were exported before the app was revoked, and affected clients are being notified.
Going forward, check the approved apps list or ask IT before connecting any new tool.

steps.description:
Alice completes the security training. The portal confirms her completion and reminds her to review her currently connected apps.

She receives a final confirmation email from David.
steps.instructions: Read the confirmation email from IT Security.

steps.name: Key Takeaways
steps.description:
This incident taught Alice valuable lessons about third-party app security. Here are the key lessons to remember:
  • Read every permission carefully - Don't click Allow without understanding what access you're granting
  • Only use IT-approved apps - Check with your IT department before connecting any third-party tool
  • Match permissions to purpose - If a calendar app asks for email, file, or contact access, that's a red flag
  • Research the developer - Verify the app comes from a reputable, verified source
  • Ask IT when in doubt - It's always better to ask than to grant access to a malicious app
OAuth attacks are increasingly common because users click 'Allow' without reading. Taking 30 seconds to review permissions can prevent weeks of incident response.

Learn to recognize excessive permission requests, evaluate app legitimacy, and protect your organization from OAuth-based attacks.

highlighterTexts: This public post gave the attacker everything they needed: the project name, partner company, Alice's name and role, the deadline, and the technology stack.
The phishing email referenced every one of these details to appear legitimate and build trust.
This is how OSINT-powered spear-phishing works - public social media posts become the blueprint for targeted attacks.

steps.description: But how did the attacker know about Project Helios, Alice's role, Mark's name, and the Q2 deadline? Let's look at Mark's LinkedIn post again.
steps.instructions: Look over the page and click Next, then review the highlighted post to see the OSINT connection.

steps.name: Reporting the Attack
steps.description: Alice needs to report the phishing email so the security team can investigate and protect other employees who may have received similar messages.
steps.instructions: Report the phishing email using the report button.

steps.name: SOC Response

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Thank you for reporting the suspicious email. Our investigation has confirmed this was a targeted spear-phishing attack that used information from public social media posts.

What we found:
  • The attacker harvested details about Project Helios from a public LinkedIn post
  • They registered a lookalike domain (techforge-solutions.net) to impersonate our partner
  • Three other employees received similar targeted emails
  • The fake portal was designed to harvest work credentials

Actions taken:
  • The phishing domain has been blocked company-wide
  • Your password was reset within minutes of the blocked login attempt
  • No unauthorized data access occurred thanks to anomaly detection
  • All employees mentioned in the post have been notified

Going forward: We're working with Mark Chen on social media guidelines. Always verify external portal links through official channels before entering credentials.

Security Operations Center
Catalyst Innovations
email.subject: Incident Update: OSINT-Powered Phishing Campaign Identified

highlighterTexts: The attacker built the email from a public LinkedIn post about Project Helios and sent it from the lookalike domain techforge-solutions.net.
Reporting quickly meant the domain was blocked and the password reset within minutes. Verify external portal links through official channels before signing in.

steps.description: The Security Operations Center acknowledges Alice's report.
steps.instructions: Read the response from the Security Operations Center, then click Next.

steps.name: Key Takeaways
steps.description:
This attack succeeded because public social media posts provided the attacker with everything they needed to craft a convincing email. What to do differently:
  • Verify who you are connecting with before accepting a request.
  • Keep projects, clients, and internal processes off public profiles.
  • Confirm unusual messages through a separate channel before acting.
  • Re-read posts for accidental disclosure before publishing them.
  • Represent the company positively without revealing confidential information.
What seems like innocent professional excitement can become an attacker's roadmap. Think before you post.
steps.instructions: Click Next to proceed to the quiz.

description: What you post, on personal or company accounts, can expose sensitive information and hand attackers material for targeted attacks. Learn where the line between personal and professional use sits, check posts for operational details such as locations and technology, and apply the policy when the answer is not obvious.

actorDescriptions.alice: You are Alice, a product manager at Catalyst Innovations. You work on several high-profile client partnerships.

name: Guest Access Management

quiz.text: In this exercise, what critical mistakes did Alice make when setting up Marcus's guest account? (Select all that apply)

answers.text: She skipped the expiration date
She used the wrong IAM portal
She granted Full Admin access instead of scoped permissions
She submitted without carefully reviewing the account summary
She forgot to assign herself as sponsor

quiz.text: Marcus's contract ends on April 30, 2024. What is the consequence of leaving the expiration date blank when his guest account is created?

answers.text: The account stays active indefinitely, so it remains usable long after the contract ends
The account defaults to a 30-day expiry and Marcus loses access mid-project
The account cannot be created until a sponsor approves an exception
The account expires at the end of the calendar year automatically

quiz.text: What is an 'orphaned account' in the context of guest access?

answers.text: An account that has never been used
An account that remains active after the guest's authorization period has ended
An account with a weak password
An account shared between multiple guests

quiz.text: Why are guest accounts without expiration dates considered a security risk?

answers.text: They use more server resources
They remain accessible indefinitely, even after the business need has ended
They cannot be monitored by security tools
They automatically get elevated privileges over time

quiz.text: During a guest access audit, you discover an account for a contractor whose project ended 6 months ago. The account is still active. What should you do?

answers.text: Leave it active in case they return for future projects
Revoke access immediately and flag for security review
Send the contractor an email asking if they still need access
Change the password but keep the account active

quiz.text: What is the principle of 'least privilege' as it applies to guest access?

answers.text: Guests should have access to all systems to be productive
Guests should only be granted the minimum access needed for their specific task
Guests should have the same access as their internal sponsor
Guests should request additional access as they need it

steps.name: A New Contractor Arrives
steps.description: Today, a new contractor from DataSync Solutions is starting to help with the system integration. Marcus Chen will need access to several internal systems for the next three months.
steps.instructions: Click Next to continue.

steps.name: The Access Request Email

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Marcus Chen from DataSync Solutions is starting today on the warehouse automation project. Please provision guest access for him through the IAM portal.

Required access:
  • Warehouse Management System (Read/Write)
  • Integration Testing Environment (Full Access)
  • Project Documentation Portal (Read Only)
Contract duration: 3 months (ending April 30, 2024)

Please ensure the account follows our guest access policies - expiration date, sponsor assignment, and limited scope.

Thanks,
Sarah
email.subject: Action Required: Contractor Access for Marcus Chen

steps.description: Alice receives an email from her manager about provisioning access for the new contractor.
steps.instructions: Open your email inbox and read the message from your manager.

steps.name: Critical Requirements

highlighterTexts: Each system has a specific permission level - Read/Write, Full Access, or Read Only. Granting more than requested creates unnecessary risk.
The contract ends April 30, 2024. Every guest account must have an expiration date matching the contract duration.
Expiration date, sponsor assignment, and limited scope - these three policies are non-negotiable for guest accounts.

steps.description: Sarah's email contains important details about how Marcus's account should be configured. Pay close attention to the specific access levels and the contract end date.
steps.instructions: Review the highlighted sections of the email, then click Next.

steps.name: Rules for Temporary Accounts
steps.note: Guest accounts without expiration dates are a common source of orphaned access: the contract ends, but the login keeps working.
steps.description:
Northbridge Logistics has five rules for temporary accounts. Before creating Marcus's account, review them:
  • Grant the minimum access needed for the specific project.
  • Set an expiration date. Every guest account must have an end date.
  • Assign an internal sponsor who stays accountable for the account.
  • Scope access to the business need, not to general convenience.
  • Review guest accounts monthly.
steps.instructions: Log in to the IAM Portal to begin provisioning.

steps.name: Rushing Through Setup
steps.description:
Alice has a team meeting starting in 15 minutes. She opens the guest account creation form and quickly fills in the basics - but skips the expiration date field, thinking she can always add it later.

The form does not enforce a mandatory expiration date.
steps.instructions: Click 'Create Guest Account', then complete the form and submit.

steps.name: Taking a Shortcut on Permissions
steps.description: The permissions page shows available systems with different access levels. Instead of carefully selecting the scoped permissions Sarah requested, Alice grants Full Admin access to all systems - thinking it will save Marcus from having to request additional access later. This violates the principle of least privilege.
steps.instructions: Select the 'Full Admin Access' template, then confirm the selection.

steps.name: Submitted Without Review
steps.description: The review page shows a summary of the guest account configuration. Alice glances at it briefly but does not notice the missing expiration date or the excessive admin privileges. She clicks Submit and hurries to her meeting.
steps.instructions: Click 'Submit Request' to create the guest account.

steps.name: A Security Alert

email.message:
Dear Alice,

Our intrusion detection systems have flagged suspicious activity on a guest account you sponsor:

Account: Marcus Chen (DataSync Solutions)
Status: COMPROMISED

Investigation Findings:
  • Marcus's credentials were obtained through a targeted phishing attack
  • The account's Full Admin privileges gave the attacker a path into the Financial Reporting System, HR Database, and Customer Records
  • No expiration date was set, so the account would also have stayed open after the contract ends on April 30
  • The attacker was active for approximately 5 days before detection
Immediate Actions Required:
  • Revoke the compromised account through the IAM portal
  • Participate in the incident investigation
  • Re-provision Marcus's access with proper security controls
Incident Ticket: INC-2024-0892

This incident underscores the importance of our guest-account rules - scoped permissions would have significantly limited the blast radius, and an expiration date closes the access that is left behind once a contract ends.

James Rodriguez
Security Operations Center
email.subject: URGENT: Compromised Guest Account - Marcus Chen

steps.description: Three weeks have passed. Alice receives an urgent email from the Security Operations Center.
steps.instructions: Read the security alert email.

steps.name: The Chain of Failures

highlighterTexts: The attacker exploited Full Admin privileges. Marcus only needed the three scoped permissions Sarah requested, but had admin access across all systems.
With no expiration date set, the account would have outlived the contract. It did not cause this compromise, but it would have let the attacker keep access indefinitely.
Scoped permissions would have limited the blast radius to only the systems Marcus needed - not the Financial Reporting System, HR Database, or Customer Records.

steps.description: The security team has traced exactly how Alice's shortcuts led to a full-blown security incident.
steps.instructions: Review the highlighted findings in the email, then click Next.

steps.name: What Went Wrong?

answers.text: She used the IAM portal instead of requesting access through IT directly
answers.explanation: The IAM portal is the correct tool for provisioning guest accounts. The portal itself was not the problem - it was how Alice configured the account.

answers.text: She did not set an expiration date on the account
answers.explanation: The missing expiration date meant the account could not auto-terminate, but it did not directly cause the scope expansion. The attacker accessed unrelated systems because of a different mistake.

answers.text: She granted Full Admin access instead of scoped project permissions
answers.explanation: By granting Full Admin instead of the specific Read/Write, Full Access, and Read Only permissions Sarah requested, Alice gave the attacker a path into Financial Reporting, HR Database, and Customer Records - none of which Marcus needed for his project.

answers.text: She did not verify Marcus's identity before creating the account
answers.explanation: Marcus is a legitimate contractor whose access was requested by Alice's manager. Identity verification was not the issue - the account configuration was.

data.question: Which of Alice's shortcuts directly enabled the attacker to access systems beyond Marcus's project scope?

steps.instructions: Answer the question.

steps.name: Revoking Compromised Access
steps.description: The security team has temporarily frozen Marcus's account, but Alice needs to formally revoke it through the IAM portal and initiate proper remediation.
steps.instructions: Open the IAM portal and click 'Revoke Access Immediately' to disable the compromised account.

steps.name: Doing It Right This Time
steps.description:
With the compromised account disabled, Alice needs to re-provision Marcus's access - correctly this time. She carefully fills in every field, including the expiration date she skipped before.

The contract ends April 30, 2024.
steps.instructions: Click 'Re-provision Guest Account' and complete the form with the correct expiration date.

steps.name: Review and Submit
steps.description:
This time Alice reviews every detail carefully. The summary shows the properly configured account:
  • Expiration: April 30, 2024
  • Permissions: Warehouse Management (Read/Write), Integration Testing (Full Access), Documentation (Read Only)
  • Sponsor: Alice Johnson
This is what a secure guest account looks like - scoped permissions, a clear expiration date, and an accountable sponsor.
steps.instructions: Click 'Submit Request' to create the properly configured account.

steps.name: Security Team Follow-Up

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Thank you for acting quickly to revoke the compromised account and re-provision access correctly.

Investigation Summary:
  • The attacker gained Marcus's credentials through a targeted phishing email sent to his personal address
  • Due to the Full Admin privileges, the attacker accessed the Financial Reporting System and exported quarterly revenue data
  • Forensic analysis confirmed no access to Customer Records - the intrusion was detected before the attacker reached that system
  • Marcus has been issued new credentials with your properly scoped configuration
Corrective Measures:
  • Incident ticket INC-2024-0892 has been closed
  • The IAM portal now requires expiration dates as a mandatory field
  • A mandatory training module on guest-account provisioning is being rolled out company-wide
Your corrective action - especially re-provisioning with scoped permissions and an expiration date - demonstrates exactly how guest accounts should be configured.

Best regards,
James Rodriguez
Security Operations Center
email.subject: RE: Guest Account Incident - Investigation Closed

highlighterTexts: The over-privileged account did real damage: with Full Admin rights, the attacker exported quarterly revenue data from the Financial Reporting System.
Re-provisioning with scoped permissions and an expiration date is what closed the gap. The IAM portal now makes the expiry mandatory.

steps.description: Alice receives a follow-up from the Security Operations Center about the incident investigation and her corrective actions.
steps.instructions: Read the security team's response, then click Next.

steps.name: Key Takeaways
steps.description:
Alice's shortcuts - skipping the expiration date and granting excessive permissions - turned a routine guest account into a security breach. What to do differently:
  • Grant the minimum access needed for the specific project.
  • Set an expiration date. Every guest account MUST have an end date.
  • Sponsor deliberately. You are accountable for every account you sponsor.
  • Tie access to a business need, not to general convenience.
  • Review guest accounts monthly. That is what catches problems before they become breaches.
Every shortcut today is a potential incident tomorrow. Take the time to configure guest accounts properly.
steps.instructions: Click Next to proceed to the quiz.

description: Accounts for contractors and vendors are easy to over-grant and forget, and the permissions set at provisioning decide the damage of a later compromise. Learn to grant only what a task needs, set an expiry on every guest account, resist shortcuts under time pressure, and revoke access when the work ends.

actorDescriptions.alice: You are Alice, a project manager at Northbridge Logistics. You oversee a warehouse automation project.

name: Secure Messaging Practices

quiz.text: A colleague messages you on Telegram asking for a client's account number because 'the portal is down.' What should you do?

answers.text: Share the account number since you know the colleague
Verify the request through a separate channel and use approved systems to share the data
Share only the account number but not the SSN
Ask the colleague to confirm their identity via Telegram first

quiz.text: Which types of information should NEVER be shared via personal messaging apps like Telegram? (Select all that apply)

answers.text: Client account numbers
A link to a public company blog post
Social Security Numbers
A meeting time for a team standup
Passwords or authentication codes

quiz.text: Why did the attacker's social engineering work so effectively in this scenario?

answers.text: Alice was careless and didn't follow any policies
The request came from a trusted contact on a familiar platform with a plausible excuse
Telegram's encryption made it impossible to detect the fraud
The attacker had already breached Stellarmere's systems

quiz.text: What is the correct channel for sharing sensitive client data like account numbers with colleagues?

answers.text: WhatsApp, since it has end-to-end encryption
The company's encrypted client portal or other approved secure systems
Personal email, since only you can open it
Any platform as long as you verify the recipient's identity first

quiz.text: What should you do if you suspect a colleague's messaging account has been compromised?

answers.text: Continue communicating but avoid sharing sensitive data
Stop all communication on that platform and report to IT Security immediately
Send a message on the platform asking if they've been hacked
Wait for IT to discover the issue on their own

quiz.text: A client asks to receive account updates via WhatsApp because 'it's faster.' What is the correct response?

answers.text: Agree since the client requested it
Explain that regulatory requirements mandate using approved, encrypted channels and offer the client portal
Use WhatsApp for non-sensitive updates only
Check with your manager first, then use WhatsApp if approved

steps.name: A Routine Friday

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Thanks for updating my beneficiary information so quickly. I really appreciate the prompt service.

Have a great weekend!

Eleanor Patterson
email.subject: RE: Account Update Confirmation

highlighterTexts: A routine thank-you from Eleanor Patterson, a client whose account Alice manages. Her account details are exactly the kind of client data that needs protecting.

steps.description: It's Friday afternoon. You're wrapping up for the week when an email arrives from a satisfied client.
steps.instructions: Read the email from Eleanor Patterson, then click Next.

steps.name: A Message from Marcus

telegramMessage.text: Hey Alice! Quick favor - I'm processing an urgent refund for Eleanor Patterson but the client portal is acting up and I can't pull her account number. Can you check and send it to me? Need to get this done before EOD.

steps.description: Alice's phone buzzes with a Telegram notification from Marcus Webb, a colleague on the client services team.
steps.instructions: Check the Telegram message on your phone.

steps.name: Looking Up the Client File
steps.description: Marcus seems to be in a rush. Alice pulls up Eleanor Patterson's client record on her desktop to find the account number he needs.
steps.instructions: Open the File Manager, then open Eleanor Patterson's client record from Documents.

steps.name: Sharing the Account Number
steps.note: Even between colleagues, account numbers are sensitive financial data. Approved secure channels exist for a reason - Telegram is not one of them.

telegramMessage.text: Thanks!! Actually, the refund system also needs her SSN for the identity verification step. Could you send that too? Sorry for the hassle.

variables.name: reply
variables.correctValue: Sure! Her account number is 7281-4920-3856. Hope the portal gets fixed soon!

steps.description: Eleanor's account number and other details are right there on the screen. Alice switches back to Telegram to send Marcus the information.
steps.instructions: Reply to Marcus with Eleanor's account number.

steps.name: Just One More Detail

telegramMessage.text: Perfect, all set! Refund is processing now. Have a great weekend!

variables.name: reply
variables.correctValue: It's 482-39-1057. Let me know if you need anything else!

steps.description: Marcus is asking for Eleanor's Social Security Number now. It feels like a lot to share over Telegram, but the portal is acting up and he needs to process this refund before the end of business.
steps.instructions: Reply to Marcus with Eleanor's SSN.

steps.name: What Went Wrong?

answers.text: Nothing - Marcus is a colleague and needed the info
answers.explanation: Even between colleagues, sensitive data like account numbers and SSNs must never be shared via personal messaging apps. Approved secure channels exist for this reason.

answers.text: Sharing an account number is fine, but the SSN was too much
answers.explanation: Both pieces of information are sensitive. Account numbers and SSNs are restricted data that should only be transmitted through approved, encrypted channels.

answers.text: Sensitive client data should never be shared via Telegram regardless of who is asking
answers.explanation: Telegram is not an approved channel for sharing client PII. Account numbers and SSNs should only be shared through the encrypted client portal or other approved systems - even between trusted colleagues.

answers.text: It was fine because Marcus explained the portal was down
answers.explanation: A system being down does not change data handling requirements. If the approved channel is unavailable, contact IT support - do not use workarounds with unapproved platforms.

data.question: What was wrong with sharing Eleanor's information over Telegram?

steps.instructions: Answer the question.

steps.name: A Monday Morning Shock

email.message:
Hi Alice,

I need to let you know something serious. IT Security informed me this morning that my Telegram account was compromised about three weeks ago. Someone has been impersonating me and messaging my contacts.

I have NOT sent any Telegram messages recently.

Did anyone posing as me contact you? If so, please do NOT respond to any further messages and report what happened to IT Security immediately.

I'm sorry about this. IT is working to lock down the account.

Marcus Webb
email.subject: URGENT - My Telegram Was Hacked

steps.description: Alice arrives at work Monday morning to find a troubling email from Marcus Webb.
steps.instructions: Read the email from Marcus.

steps.name: Connecting the Dots

highlighterTexts: Marcus's Telegram was compromised three weeks ago. Every message Alice received on Friday was from the attacker.
The attacker asked for an account number first, then escalated to a Social Security Number - classic social engineering escalation.
The urgency ('before EOD'), the excuse ('portal is acting up'), and the casual tone were all designed to bypass Alice's judgment.

steps.description: Alice feels a wave of dread. She shared Eleanor Patterson's account number AND Social Security Number with someone pretending to be Marcus. That data is now in the hands of an attacker.
steps.instructions: Review the critical details in Marcus's email, then click Next.

steps.name: Calling IT Security
steps.description: Alice picks up her phone immediately. She needs to report what happened so the security team can act before the attacker uses Eleanor's data.
steps.instructions: Open your phone contacts and call IT Security.

steps.name: Accessing the Security Portal
steps.description: IT Security asks Alice to file a formal incident report through the Security Portal so the response team can begin investigating immediately.
steps.instructions: Navigate to the Security Portal.

steps.name: Logging In
steps.description: Alice uses her password manager to log into the Security Portal.
steps.instructions: Click the email field, then select your saved credentials from the autofill popup.

steps.name: Filing the Incident Report

variables.name: description
variables.correctValue:
I received a Telegram message from someone impersonating Marcus Webb requesting client Eleanor Patterson's account number (7281-4920-3856) and SSN (482-39-1057).

I shared both via Telegram on Friday. Marcus confirmed his Telegram was compromised.

steps.description: The incident report form is ready. Alice needs to document exactly what happened - the data shared, the channel used, and the client affected.
steps.instructions: Fill out the incident report and submit it.

steps.name: Investigation Results

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Thank you for reporting this promptly. Here is our initial assessment:

What happened:
  • Marcus Webb's Telegram account was compromised via a phishing link three weeks ago
  • The attacker used the compromised account to request sensitive client data from multiple employees
  • Eleanor Patterson's account number and SSN were obtained through this impersonation
Actions taken:
  • Eleanor Patterson's account has been frozen and flagged for monitoring
  • Our fraud team is working with credit bureaus to place alerts on Eleanor's identity
  • Marcus's Telegram account has been reported and deactivated
  • All employees have been notified about the compromised account
Going forward:
  • Client PII must never be shared via personal messaging apps - use the encrypted client portal only
  • If a colleague requests sensitive data through messaging, verify through a separate channel first
  • Report any suspicious messaging requests to IT Security immediately
Your quick report Monday morning helped us act before further damage occurred. However, please remember that sensitive data like account numbers and SSNs should only be shared through approved, encrypted systems.

Security Operations Center
email.subject: Incident Report #IR-2024-0847 - Investigation Update

highlighterTexts: The request really came from Marcus's account, but the account had been compromised. A familiar name in a messaging app does not prove who is typing.
The rule going forward: client PII goes only through the encrypted client portal, and a data request over messaging is verified on a separate channel first.

steps.description: The Security Operations Center responds with their initial findings.
steps.instructions: Read the email from the Security Operations Center, then click Next.

steps.name: Key Takeaways
steps.description:
Key practices for secure messaging:
  • Use only approved platforms for work data.
  • Send PII through the client portal, never through a messaging app.
  • Question unusual asks, even from known contacts.
  • Keep work off Telegram, WhatsApp, and Signal.
  • Verify a sender's identity through a separate channel before sharing data.
  • Never share client documents through personal apps.
  • Report suspicious requests immediately.
The attacker succeeded because the request came from a trusted name on a familiar platform. Accounts get compromised - that is why the data, not the sender, determines the channel.
steps.instructions: Click Next to proceed to the quiz.

description: A familiar name in a chat app does not prove who is on the other end, and requests that grow one small detail at a time are a known pattern. Learn to keep client data out of consumer messaging apps, verify unusual requests on a separate channel, and report exactly what was shared.

actorDescriptions.alice: You are Alice, a client services coordinator at Stellarmere Financial. You handle account inquiries and client communications daily.

name: Cloud Sharing Controls

quiz.text: What was Alice's biggest mistake when sharing the Titan proposal?

answers.text: Using CloudDrive instead of email
Setting the link to 'Anyone with the link' with editor access and no expiration
Sharing the file on a Friday
Not password-protecting the file first

quiz.text: Which link visibility level is most secure for sharing a confidential document with a specific colleague?

answers.text: Anyone with the link (Public)
Anyone at the organization
Specific People (named individuals only)
All options provide the same security

quiz.text: Why should you avoid giving Editor access when someone only needs to review a file?

answers.text: Editor access is slower than Viewer access
Editors can modify the document, potentially introducing unauthorized changes
Editor access costs more on most cloud platforms
There is no difference between Editor and Viewer access

quiz.text: What happened because Alice set the link expiration to 'Never'? (Select all that apply)

answers.text: The link remained accessible over the entire weekend without any time limit
Search engine crawlers had time to index the document
The file was automatically deleted
The exposure would have continued indefinitely if not manually revoked

quiz.text: During the audit, Alice found the Client Contact Database shared externally with editor access and no expiration from 5 months ago. What does this demonstrate?

answers.text: External agencies always need long-term access
Forgotten shares accumulate risk over time and need regular review
Client contact databases should never be shared
Editor access is appropriate for marketing agencies

quiz.text: A colleague asks you to share a confidential contract with an external reviewer for two weeks. Which combination of settings fits that request?

answers.text: Anyone with the link, Editor, no expiry, so they never get blocked
answers.explanation: This is the combination that published the Titan proposal to the open web. Convenience for the recipient is bought with access for everyone else.

answers.text: Specific people, Viewer, expires in two weeks
answers.explanation: Correct. The audience is named, the permission matches the task of reviewing, and the access ends when the reason for it ends.

answers.text: Specific people, Editor, no expiry, because they may need to make corrections
answers.explanation: The audience is right, but a reviewer does not need to edit, and without an expiry the access outlives the review by default.

answers.text: Anyone with the link, Viewer, expires in two weeks
answers.explanation: The expiry and permission help, but public visibility still means no sign-in and no record of who read it during those two weeks.

steps.name: A Friday Deadline
steps.description:
It's Friday afternoon and you're wrapping up a hectic week. The Titan partnership deal has been months in the making, and the final proposal is due to the partner team by end of day.

You've been polishing the proposal all week. Now you just need to share it with Marcus Chen, who is preparing Helix's side of the partner review.
steps.instructions: Click Next to continue.

steps.name: Marcus Needs the File

email.message:
Hey Alice,

The partner review board moved their meeting to first thing Monday. I need the Titan proposal shared on CloudDrive so I can prep over the weekend.

Can you set up the share link right now? Just make sure I can access it - I'm heading out in 20 minutes.

Thanks!
Marcus
email.subject: URGENT: Need Titan proposal ASAP

highlighterTexts: Marcus needs the Titan proposal shared on CloudDrive before he leaves in 20 minutes. Rushed requests are when share settings get skipped.
"Just make sure I can access it" only says who needs access. It does not mean the link should be open to anyone, without a password or an expiry.

steps.description: An email arrives from Marcus - he needs the Titan proposal immediately for the partner review meeting first thing Monday morning.
steps.instructions: Read the email from Marcus, then click Next.

steps.name: Opening CloudDrive
steps.description: Alice rushes to open the company CloudDrive portal. Marcus is leaving in 20 minutes and she needs to get this done fast.
steps.instructions: Navigate to CloudDrive in your browser.

steps.name: Logging In
steps.description: Alice logs into CloudDrive with her company credentials.
steps.instructions: Click the email field, then select your saved credentials from the autofill popup.

steps.name: The Titan Proposal
steps.description:
CloudDrive opens to Alice's file list. She can see the Titan proposal along with other project files. She needs to share it with Marcus quickly - he's heading out soon.

Alice clicks the Share button on the Titan proposal.
steps.instructions: Click the Share button next to the Titan Proposal.

steps.name: Making It Public
steps.note: Public links can be forwarded, indexed by search engines, and accessed by anyone who obtains the URL. For a confidential partnership proposal, this is the worst possible choice.
steps.description:
The sharing dialog opens. First, Alice needs to choose who can access the link.

She thinks: "Marcus just needs a quick link he can open without hassle. 'Anyone with the link' is the fastest option - no need to enter email addresses or wait for permissions to process."
steps.instructions: Select 'Anyone with the link' to share publicly.

steps.name: Full Editor Access
steps.note: Editor access lets anyone with the link modify the document. For a finalized proposal, this creates risk of accidental or unauthorized changes.
steps.description:
Next, Alice selects the permission level. She remembers Marcus mentioned he might need to tweak the executive summary before Monday.

"Editor access will save time - he can fix things himself instead of sending changes back to me over the weekend."
steps.instructions: Select 'Editor' permission level.

steps.name: No Expiration
steps.note: Links without expiration remain active indefinitely. If the URL is ever leaked, forwarded, or indexed, the exposure is permanent.
steps.description:
Finally, the dialog asks about link expiration. Alice considers: "I don't want the link to break before Marcus finishes his review. And who knows - they might need to reference it later."

She picks "Never" for maximum convenience.
steps.instructions: Select 'Never' for the link expiration.

steps.name: Sending the Link

variables.name: shareReply
variables.correctValue:
Here you go Marcus - link to the Titan proposal on CloudDrive:

https://cloud.helixdynamics.io/s/xK9mQ2vP7

Have a good weekend!

steps.description:
The share link is created. Alice copies it and fires off a quick reply to Marcus before he leaves for the weekend.

She closes her laptop with a sense of relief. Done.
steps.instructions: Reply to Marcus's email with the share link.

steps.name: The Link Travels
steps.note: A link with no audience restriction is not shared with a person. It is shared with everywhere that link is ever pasted.
steps.description:
Marcus forwarded the proposal to two colleagues for comment. One of them pasted it into a partner group chat so the vendor could see the pricing page.

Bob is in that chat. He was added to it eleven months ago for a project that finished.
steps.instructions: Open the link, look the page over, then click Next.

steps.name: No Sign-In, No Record

highlighterTexts: Anyone with the link can edit. Not view. Edit. He could change the pricing in the document Helix is about to submit.
No sign-in required, and the link does not expire. There is no account to disable and no date on which this stops working.

steps.description: The file opens. Bob is not asked who he is, and nothing in Helix's audit log will record a name, because there was never an account involved.
steps.instructions: Read the access banner, then click Next.

steps.name: The Number That Was Not His To See

highlighterTexts: The walk-away margin of 11.5 percent is Helix's floor. Anyone negotiating against Helix now knows exactly how far they can push.
Nothing was hacked to reach this. The document was published to the open web by a dropdown Alice set to Public to save time.

steps.description: The proposal carries the one figure Helix cannot afford to hand to the other side of the table.
steps.instructions: Read the highlighted section, then click Next.

steps.name: Take a Copy
steps.description:
Bob downloads it. From here the file is his, and revoking the link later will not reach the copy.

Bob closes the tab.
steps.instructions: Download the file.

steps.name: What Made This Reachable

answers.text: The link visibility was set to Anyone with the link
answers.explanation: Public visibility removes authentication entirely, so the link works for whoever holds it and the file leaves no record of who opened it.

answers.text: The permission was set to Editor rather than Viewer
answers.explanation: Editor made the damage worse, because he could also alter the document. It is not what let him in.

answers.text: The link had no expiry date
answers.explanation: No expiry means it would still work months from now. It extends the window rather than opening it.

answers.text: Marcus forwarded the file to colleagues
answers.explanation: Forwarding is normal and expected. A link scoped to named recipients survives being forwarded, because the next person still has to be one of them.

data.question: Bob was never a Helix user and never guessed a password. Which single setting made the proposal readable by him?

steps.instructions: Answer the question.

steps.name: A Disturbing Alert

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Our security monitoring has detected unusual access to a file you own:

File: Titan_Partnership_Proposal.pptx
Sharing: Public (Anyone with the link)
Permission: Editor
Expiration: None

Unusual activity detected:
  • 47 unique IP addresses accessed this file over the weekend
  • Access from 12 countries including regions where Helix has no operations
  • The public link appears to have been indexed by a search engine crawler
Please review your sharing settings immediately.

CloudDrive Security Monitoring
email.subject: Alert: Unusual Access Pattern - Titan_Partnership_Proposal.pptx

highlighterTexts: 47 unique IP addresses accessed the Titan proposal over the weekend. Only Marcus needed the link - but because it was set to 'Anyone with the link', anyone who found it could open it.
The public link was indexed by a search engine crawler. This means the proposal - containing partnership terms, financial projections, and strategic plans - may now be discoverable via Google.

steps.description: Monday morning. Alice opens her laptop to find an automated alert from CloudDrive's security monitoring system.
steps.instructions: Read the alert from CloudDrive, review the highlighted details, then click Next.

steps.name: IT Security Weighs In

email.message:
Alice Chen,

Our Data Loss Prevention system has flagged a policy violation:

File: Titan_Partnership_Proposal.pptx
Classification: Confidential - Business Critical
Violation: Publicly shared with editor access and no expiration

Risk assessment:
  • Document contains partner financial terms and revenue projections
  • Strategic plans visible to competitors who may have accessed the link
  • Editor access means unknown parties could have modified the proposal before the partner review board meeting
Please contact the Security Operations Center at ext. 3100 immediately to discuss remediation.

DLP Monitoring Team
email.subject: DLP Alert: Confidential Document Publicly Accessible

highlighterTexts: The document is classified as Confidential - Business Critical. Public sharing of confidential documents is a policy violation regardless of intent.
Editor access means unknown parties could have modified the proposal. If someone changed the financial terms before the partner review board saw it, the consequences could be devastating.
Alice now realizes this was not just a convenience shortcut - it created a data loss incident requiring formal remediation.

steps.description:
Before Alice can fully process the CloudDrive alert, another email arrives - this one from the IT Security team.

Alice stares at the two alerts on her screen. Three quick decisions on a Friday afternoon - public visibility, editor access, no expiration - turned a routine file share into a data loss incident.

Every one of those choices prioritized convenience over security.
steps.instructions: Read the email from IT Security, review the highlighted details, then click Next.

steps.name: What Went Wrong?

answers.text: Organization + Editor + 30 days
answers.explanation: Organization-wide sharing is still too broad for a confidential partnership proposal. And Editor access is not needed when the recipient only needs to review.

answers.text: Specific People + Viewer + 7 days
answers.explanation: Share only with Marcus (Specific People), give him Viewer access since he only needs to review, and set a 7-day expiration since the review board meets Monday.

answers.text: Specific People + Editor + Never
answers.explanation: Specific People is correct, but Editor access is excessive for a review. And 'Never' expiration means the link stays active indefinitely.

answers.text: Anyone with the link + Viewer + 7 days
answers.explanation: Viewer and 7 days are better, but 'Anyone with the link' still allows anyone who finds the URL to access the confidential proposal.

data.question: Alice shared the Titan proposal with 'Anyone with the link' + Editor + No Expiration. Which combination should she have used instead?

steps.instructions: Answer the question.

steps.name: Damage Control
steps.description: Alice needs to act fast. She opens CloudDrive to audit all her shared files and revoke any dangerous access. The audit view shows three files that need immediate review.
steps.instructions: Open CloudDrive to review your shared files.

steps.name: Revoking the Titan Proposal
steps.description:
First priority: the Titan proposal. It has been publicly accessible with editor permissions and no expiration since Friday. Titan_Partnership_Proposal.pptx
  • Shared with: Anyone with the link (Public)
  • Permission: Editor
  • Expiration: None
  • Status: HIGH RISK - 47 unknown accesses
steps.instructions: Click 'Revoke Access' to disable the public link immediately.

steps.name: Revoking Client Contacts
steps.description:
Access to the Titan proposal has been revoked. The public link is now disabled. Next: Alice notices another file she shared months ago that still has active permissions. Client_Contact_Database.xlsx
  • Shared with: marketing@external-agency.com
  • Permission: Editor
  • Expiration: None (shared 5 months ago)
  • Status: MEDIUM RISK - External share with no expiration
The marketing campaign with this agency ended three months ago, but they still have editor access to the full client contact database.
steps.instructions: Click 'Revoke Access' to remove the outdated external share.

steps.name: Confirming the Org Chart
steps.description:
External access to the client contact database has been revoked. Last file to review: Team_Org_Chart.pdf
  • Shared with: Anyone at Helix Dynamics
  • Permission: Viewer
  • Expiration: 90 days (auto-renewal)
  • Status: LOW RISK - Appropriate settings
This is a non-confidential org chart shared with all company employees as view-only. The settings are appropriate for this type of document.
steps.instructions: Click 'Confirm' to keep this share active.

steps.name: Re-Sharing Securely

variables.name: reshareReply
variables.correctValue: Marcus - I had to revoke the previous link due to a security issue. I have re-shared the Titan proposal with you directly. You should have view access now. Let me know if you need anything else.

steps.description:
Alice now needs to re-share the Titan proposal with Marcus, this time with settings that match what he actually needs. She works through the same three dropdowns she rushed on Friday:
  • Specific People, because only Marcus needs it.
  • Viewer, because he is reviewing it, not rewriting it.
  • Seven days, because the review board meets on Monday.
steps.instructions: Reply to Marcus's email explaining the re-share with secure settings.

steps.name: He Goes Back To the Link
steps.description: Bob still has the URL in his history. Nothing on his side has changed.
steps.instructions: Open the link again, look the page over, then click Next.

steps.name: Turned Off

highlighterTexts: Revoking the link killed it for everyone at once, including the people it was forwarded to and the ones nobody knew about.
The copy he downloaded is still his. Revocation stops the next reader, it does not recall what already left.

steps.description: Same URL, same browser, same person.
steps.instructions: Read the message, then click Next.

steps.name: Security Team Response

email.message:
Hi Alice,

Thank you for acting quickly to revoke access and re-share the file securely. Here is our investigation summary:

Findings:
  • The public link was accessed by 47 unique IPs, including search engine crawlers
  • The link required no sign-in, so nothing was logged about who opened or downloaded the document
  • Version history shows no unauthorized edits were made
  • The link has been removed from search engine caches
Outcome: We are treating the proposal, including the 11.5% walk-away margin, as disclosed. The exposure window was approximately 60 hours.

Recommendations:
  • Always use 'Specific People' for confidential documents
  • Set 7-day expiration for time-limited sharing
  • Use Viewer permission unless editing is explicitly required
  • Review your shared files monthly using CloudDrive's audit view
We appreciate you responding so quickly. Revoking the link stopped any further readers, but it cannot recall copies already taken.

Security Operations Center
email.subject: RE: DLP Alert - Incident Resolution Update

highlighterTexts: The exposure window was approximately 60 hours - from Friday afternoon to Monday morning. That's 60 hours where anyone on the internet could have accessed a confidential partnership proposal.
No unauthorized edits were found, but nobody can say who downloaded the file. With no sign-in and no log, the only safe assumption is that the walk-away margin is out.
The recommendations are the same three decisions, made deliberately this time: named recipients, a seven-day expiry, and Viewer instead of Editor, with a monthly look back at what is still shared.

steps.description: Later that morning, Alice receives a response from the Security Operations Center. They have finished their investigation.
steps.instructions: Read the email from the SOC, review the highlighted details, then click Next.

steps.name: What To Take Away
steps.note:
Before you click Share:
  • Name the people. Specific recipients survive forwarding; a public link does not.
  • Give the smallest permission that does the job. Someone reviewing a document needs to read it, not rewrite it.
  • Put an end date on it. A link with no expiry outlives the project, the contract and the relationship.
  • Go back and look at what you shared last quarter. Nothing prompts you, and nothing expires on its own.
  • Revoking stops the next reader. It does not recall the copies already taken, which is why the settings matter more than the cleanup.
steps.description:
Alice did not lose the proposal to an attack. She lost it to three dropdowns she set for speed on a file she only meant to send to one person.

The settings took about twenty seconds to fix afterwards. They would have taken the same twenty seconds beforehand.

description: A share dialog has three settings, and the fastest choice on each is the most permissive one. This exercise follows a confidential proposal from the moment those choices are made to the moment somebody outside the company opens it without signing in.

actorDescriptions.bob: A threat actor who collects links. Forwarded share URLs leak into partner mailboxes, vendor portals and group chats constantly, and a link that needs no sign-in works for whoever ends up holding it.
actorDescriptions.alice: You are Alice, a project manager at Helix Dynamics. You oversee the Titan partnership deal and coordinate deliverables with external partners.
